purpose: Empirical runtime scaling on nested frozen event samples; not an asymptotic complexity proof
sampling: Within each original Parquet file, order rows by exact event_id; half retains even row numbers; quarter retains row numbers divisible by four. Preserve original columns and 365-file layout. Quarter is an exact subset of half.
limitations: Full-size timings reused from preceding run; host load and cache state may differ.
Parquet file count stays fixed at 365, so fixed per-file overhead does not scale with row count.
Event thinning changes distinct cardinalities and join/funnel relationships, not just rows scanned.
Incomplete source export and missing seven-day metadata halo, as in original comparison.
Shared host; uncontrolled caches; server CPU/memory limits unchanged; DuckDB default memory limit.
Three medians over a fourfold size range only estimate local scaling, not asymptotic Big-O.
